purpose: Run the September CUDA protocol again with the card's link at PCIe generation 4 and 16 lanes, so the forecast that tools/cost_model.py --forecast committed before this run can be set beside a measurement

repeats.protocol: docs/cuda-protocol.json, whose one run on 2026-09-29 at 675bd82ad9f2ed25cda41835835a1074ebc88ace gave docs/evidence/baseline-cuda.csv
repeats.reason: on 2026-11-25 the motherboard setting for the card's slot was found at generation 3 and set to automatic, and the link has read generation 4 with 16 lanes since. No reading records the link of the September run, so this run measures the same calls at a known link, and docs/evidence/cost-model-forecast.json says beforehand what the cost model expects of it
changes: the link generation and width are part of the protocol, at generation 4 and 16 lanes
tools/run_cuda_gen4.py reads the link, the GPU utilization and the memory in use with nvidia-smi every 50 milliseconds while the benchmark runs and keeps every reading in the receipt
the samples and the receipt are named cuda-gen4.csv and cuda-gen4-execution.json, so the September files stay as they are
repeats.unchanged: the benchmark tools/cuda_benchmark.cpp, its sizes, workloads, distributions, backends, iterations, inputs, timing boundaries and CSV columns are those of docs/cuda-protocol.json

forecast.rule: committed before the first sample of this run. The run's receipt records its source revision, and the forecast's commit must be an ancestor of it

pcie_link.interval_reason: the September CUDA run took about 0.44 seconds, so the 250 milliseconds of docs/pinned-gen4-protocol.json would give one or two readings, and an idle card can read generation 1 for both
pcie_link.readings: tools/run_cuda_gen4.py starts nvidia-smi, waits for its first reading, starts the benchmark, waits after the benchmark exits until at least one more reading arrives, then stops nvidia-smi and keeps every reading in the receipt. An idle card drops its link to generation 1 to save power, so readings at generation 1 before, between and after the calls are expected and kept
pcie_link.qualifies: the same rule as docs/pinned-gen4-protocol.json. The run is passed only when the readings exist, every one gives the maximum as generation 4 with 16 lanes, every one gives the current link either as generation 4 with 16 lanes or as the idle generation 1, and at least one gives it as generation 4 with 16 lanes. A reading at generation 2 or 3, or at generation 4 with fewer lanes, would mean the link trained down while the benchmark ran, and the run is then unqualified and kept
pcie_link.side_effect: the nvidia-smi process polls the card beside every timed row, which the September run did not have

load.rule: the run goes ahead at the usual desktop load with no game running, as T decided for the SYCL comparison and the pinned run on 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-23
load.readings: the September benchmark reads the card before no call, and adding such a reading would make it another benchmark than the one the forecast predicts. The load is read instead by the same nvidia-smi process as the link, every 50 milliseconds, as GPU utilization in percent and memory in use in MiB, and by one nvidia-smi reading before and one after the run
load.label: every published result is labeled as measured on a working desktop, with the range of those readings stated beside it

preconditions: source, protocol and forecast committed before collection
native and CUDA correctness passed on the measuring computer
no game running, checked privately by the person who starts the run, while the usual desktop applications keep using the GPU
no other build, benchmark or GPU job of this computer's lanes running, which heavy.lock records
nvidia-smi gives the link maximum as generation 4 with 16 lanes before the run
first_iteration: retained separately, first invocation of condition after device discovery, not cold process
cuda_timing: events on one stream bracket H2D, kernels and D2H, and the stream is synchronized before results or memory release
host_timing: same outer steady_clock boundary for CPU and CUDA, including validation, allocations, copies, launch, synchronization, checksum selection, result destruction and CUDA cleanup
correctness: 180 rows, each condition with iterations 0 to 5 once, every timing finite and not negative, and every checksum equal across backends within 1e-8 for masked_reduce and 1e-12 otherwise, as tools/validate_evidence.py checks the September files
differences_from_september: the source is the revision the receipt names, not 675bd82, and the binary, the compilers, the CUDA toolkit and the driver are those the receipt records. src/cuda.cu changed between the two revisions, so the report states these differences beside every comparison and claims no cause for one
environment: record CPU, GPU, driver, CUDA toolkit compiler, host compiler, OS, source, protocol and binary identities, GPU state before and after, and the link and load readings in the receipt that tools/run_cuda_gen4.py writes, have the person who starts the run check the GPU processes beforehand for a game, confirm with --confirm-desktop-load that none runs and keep that list in a private record outside the repository, and preserve ordinary applications and default settings
decision: retain every result, including CUDA calls slower than the CPU and predictions that miss. The report sets each forecast beside its measurement, marks every miss over 25 percent with a reason or the words not explained, and says which of the two predictions the uploads fit better, without claiming what generation the link was at in September
historical_evidence: leave docs/cuda-protocol.json, the 504 original rows, their receipt, docs/results-2026-09-29.md, the cost model page and its CSV, and docs/evidence/cost-model-forecast.json unchanged
